content.title: Kit Builder
content.summary: Sort everyday things into your family's emergency kit, together. Talk through each choice—some supplies are basics for most households, while others depend on your family.
content.objective: Talk through which supplies most households need and which additional items fit your household.
content.facilitation: An adult reads each item aloud. Ask everyone where it belongs for your household and why. If you disagree, talk it through; the conversation is the practice.

discussed_core_kit_items.text: Your household talked through basic emergency-kit supplies together.

discussed_household_specific_needs.text: Your household considered supplies that depend on the people and pets in your home.

activity.prompt: Where does this go for your family?
activity.reminderQuestion: Did this remind you of anything your household needs?
activity.recapBody: FEMA recommends keeping basics such as water, food that doesn't need refrigeration, a flashlight, radio, first-aid kit, whistle, and phone charging backup in an emergency kit. Your household may need additional supplies too.
activity.nextNote: Opens your real home kit. Nothing changes unless you save it.
